messages:
oliver (Acme Inc.): Hey—we started seeing intermittent 400s from the embeddings batch endpoint and big latency spikes since last night. Error payload: "dimension mismatch: received 1536 expected 1024". Also noticed a billing spike. Any idea?

maya (support): Sorry about that, Oliver. Can you paste the raw request body + model name + batch_size you used? Also any trace id from the response headers would help.

oliver (Acme Inc.): Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/batch
  -H "Authorization: Bearer XXXX"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-1024-v1","inputs":["doc1","doc2", ...],"batch_size":32}'
```
Response (one example):
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{ "error": "dimension mismatch: received 1536 expected 1024", "trace_id": "trace-abc1234" }
```
It mostly fails once we cross ~8 items per batch. Smaller batches okay.

maya (support): Thanks — opening escalation. @jess can you look at the trace? @lee fyi for runtime.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-184 — Embeddings batch validation errors (link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-184) :rotating_light:

jess (eng-observability): I pulled trace-abc1234. Top-level breakdown: client-serialize 45ms, network 60ms, server/embeddings.batch-handler 1.3s, model-exec 1.15s. But the 400 comes from a validation span before model exec. That usually means one input in the batch produced a vector length that doesn't match the requested model shape.

jess (eng-observability): Two likely causes: 1) mixed model names in the same request (the client library or upstream pipeline accidentally merged inputs intended for different models), or 2) a model alias changed server-side and some partition returned a different-dim model. Can you grep your producer for model strings?

oliver (Acme Inc.): Our producer always sets model: text-embed-1024-v1 in the request. But digging into logs I see an internal microservice transformed metadata for some items — sample payload from our staging logs: 
```
{"inputs":[{"text":"...","meta":{"model":"text-embed-1536-alpha"}}, {"text":"...","meta":{"model":"text-embed-1024-v1"}}], "model":"text-embed-1024-v1"}
```
So two different model tags somehow landed in the same batch. We only recently added async aggregation, maybe a race.

lee (eng-runtime): If a batch contains multiple model variants we can't pad/convert dims on the fly; runtime validation rejects the whole request with 400. That's by design to avoid silent correctness issues. The right pattern is to group by model/dimension before sending. We'll add a clearer validation error message in the short term.

maya (support): Workarounds: 1) Group inputs by model name/dim upstream so every batch is homogeneous. 2) Reduce client batch_size to 8 while you patch the producer. 3) For tracing, add header: `X-Redwood-Trace: <client-id>-<req-id>` so we can sample and correlate quickly.

jess (eng-observability): How to view per-request latency in Console: Observability -> Traces -> paste trace id (trace-abc1234). For aggregate span breakdown use the query: `service:embeddings route:embed-batch | group_by span.name | sum(duration_ms)` in Logs Explorer. Direct link (internal): https://console.redwood.example/obs/traces/trace-abc1234

jess (eng-observability): If you want raw trace export:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" 
  "https://api.redwood.example/internal/traces/export?trace_id=trace-abc1234"
```
That returns span-level timings and the validation failure message.

oliver (Acme Inc.): Got it. Also the billing spike: we had 6 retries in our client after the 400s, that blew up cost. Any chance of a credit?

billing-bot: Billing anomaly flagged for acct-acme-123. Detected ~2.3x normal embedding units for the window 2026-02-14T22:00Z - 2026-02-15T02:00Z. Suggested temporary credit; will escalate to billing ops.

maya (support): Next steps: 1) Oliver, confirm whether your upstream aggregator is mixing model metadata (sounds like yes). 2) If confirmed, apply grouped batching + reduce client batch_size to 8 and resend test payload (share new trace id). 3) We'll coordinate billing review. 4) @lee will open a runtime ticket to improve error clarity and prevent silent mixed-model acceptance.

oliver (Acme Inc.): Confirmed — patching aggregator now to normalize metadata and group by model. I'll run a test and post a fresh trace. Thanks for the quick triage.

lee (eng-runtime): Filed RDW-558: "Reject mixed-dimension batches with explicit error + telemetry". Will PR a clearer error message and a runtime metric for mixed-batch rejects. ETA ~48h.

maya (support): Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open until we have the runtime patch and billing update. Oliver, please paste the new trace id when you have it and we'll re-check the spans. :thumbsup:
